review.summary: AGENTLESS demonstrates that a straightforward hierarchical localization-and-repair pipeline can achieve competitive repository-level issue resolution without autonomous agent interaction. Its empirical comparison, cost reporting, component analysis, and manual analysis of SWE-bench Lite problems make the paper useful both as a baseline and as a benchmark critique, while evidence is limited to one model and one benchmark setting.

observations.claim: A clear and reproducible-in-principle pipeline combines hierarchical code localization, patch sampling, test filtering, and majority voting; component results indicate these choices improve resolution.
observations.quote: AGENTLESS smartly combines existing techniques to construct an easy-to-understand approach.

observations.claim: On SWE-bench Lite, the reported result is competitive among open-source approaches and includes a comparatively low reported inference cost; the paper also separates this result from broader commercial comparisons.
The manual benchmark analysis identifies description-quality problems and proposes a filtered subset; the paper reports that the relative ranking remains broadly similar on it.
observations.quote: We refer to our subset of 252 problems as SWE-bench Lite-S.

observations.claim: The strongest evidence is narrowly scoped: the implementation is reported with GPT-4o on SWE-bench Lite, while baseline results are drawn from reported sources and some approaches cannot be independently verified from trajectories or code. Generalization to other models and settings remains unanswered.

unresolved_questions: Would the approach retain its cost and performance advantages with other LLMs, larger or multi-file repository tasks, or newer benchmark versions?
How robust and reproducible are SWE-bench Lite-S classifications and comparisons when evaluated by independent annotators and when commercial tools are run directly on the modified set?
The inspected passages do not establish whether patch sampling, filtering, and localization gains persist across repeated runs or alternative model configurations.
